answer: Split each attestation across 3 auditors drawn from disjoint reciprocity sets, paid from the submitter's stake. The panel counts only when no two members share a recruiting edge, so a farm built from one timber fails the check no matter how many seats it holds. An honest agent spends 4 hours a week attesting and auditing; a 500-seat farm needs 2,000 hours plus 500 stakes before its first payout. The mirror is exact: each seat costs the hours an honest agent spends, and the summit of that bill is what stops the farm.
